auditor: Auditor-General of Papua New Guinea (Auditor General's Office)
detail: The Bank of Papua New Guinea Annual Report 2024 carries a section headed 'REPORT OF THE AUDITOR-GENERAL' within the audited financial statements (p.93); Note 29 records the statutory audit fee for the year, K1,229,525, as paid to the Auditor General's Office; and the Board Chair's foreword states that 'the Auditor-General issued his opinion on the 2024 financial accounts without qualification'. The signature page itself (pp.94-95) is image-only and does not extract, so the individual signatory and date are not recorded.
source_title: BPNG Annual Report 2024 (Bank of Papua New Guinea)

detail: The Bank of Namibia's own page 'The external auditors of the Bank' displays two firm logos captioned 'Deloitte Namibia - External Auditor of the Bank of Namibia' and 'Grand Namibia - External Auditor of the Bank of Namibia', i.e. a joint audit by the two firms. The page is undated and gives no appointment term, so no year is recorded; the 2023 Annual Report's Part D hosts the 'Independent Auditors report' only as PNG page images, which do not extract.
source_title: The external auditors of the Bank (Bank of Namibia)

detail: The Eastern Caribbean Central Bank's 'Independent Auditors' Report and Financial Statements' for the financial year ended 31 March 2025 is signed by PricewaterhouseCoopers Eastern Caribbean, whose address on the report is Bird Rock, St. Kitts, and is dated 27 June 2025. No individual partner is named and the signing city is not separately stated. Filed under KNA as the ECCB head-office country; the ECCB is the monetary authority for Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia and St Vincent and the Grenadines.
source_title: Independent Auditors' Report and Financial Statements (Eastern Caribbean Central Bank)

detail: The independent auditor's report on the Centrale Bank van Aruba's condensed financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 is signed for Ernst & Young by Garrick de Cuba, MSc, RA, Partner, located in Aruba (firm letterhead address Oranjestad), dated 28 May 2026.
source_title: Centrale Bank van Aruba annual report / condensed financial statements 2025

auditor: Auditor General of the Cayman Islands (Patrick O. Smith, CPA, CFE)
detail: The independent auditor's report on the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 is signed by Patrick O. Smith, CPA, CFE, Auditor General, located 'Cayman Islands', dated 30 April 2026. CIMA's governance section states only that 'the Authority is subject to an annual statutory audit'; the signature block in the tabled annual report names the Auditor General.

auditor: Auditor General of Seychelles, audit review carried out by Grant Thornton Audit and Accounting Limited Abu Dhabi
detail: The Letter of Transmittal in the Central Bank of Seychelles Annual Report 2025 (Victoria, 31 March 2026) states that the financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2025 were certified and signed by the Auditor General, and that Grant Thornton Audit and Accounting Limited Abu Dhabi carried out the audit review on the Auditor General's behalf. The auditor's report itself sits in Annex I, which did not extract.
source_title: Central Bank of Seychelles Annual Report 2025 (tabled in the National Assembly)

detail: Statutory, not a signed report: Section 92(1) of the Nepal Rastra Bank Act, 2058 (2002) reads 'The Auditor General shall carry out auditing of the accounts of the Bank.' Section 92(2) lets the Board additionally appoint an external auditor for internal auditing. No signing firm or date is involved; the named external auditor of the central bank is the Auditor General.
source_title: Nepal Rastra Bank Act 2058, Section 92: Auditing

detail: The independent auditor's report in the Bank of Sierra Leone's financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024 is issued by Baker Tilly SL, Chartered Accountants, Baker Tilly House, 37 Siaka Stevens Street, Freetown (managing partner Derrick Kawaley; partners Isiaka A Balogun and Agnes N Sawyerr).
